title: Medication Relief Credit for Members with Regular Refills
content:
The medication relief credit lowers the cost-sharing cap of a Medicaid Managed Care Membership member whose Pharmacy Benefit shows regular refills. Where the Pharmacy Benefit shows at least 5 paid refills dated in the counting window and no rejected fill in that window, the credit is 60.00 USD; where it shows at least 5 paid refills and at least one rejected fill in the window, the credit is 30.00 USD; otherwise there is no medication relief. The credit is subtracted from the member's cap as that cap stands after it is rounded to the cent.

## Basis questions

**What counts as a paid refill?** A fill on the member's Pharmacy Benefit fill history that was dispensed as a refill, with a fill date in the counting window. A first fill of a new prescription is not a refill, and a rejected fill is not a paid refill.

**What counts as a rejected fill?** Any fill the Pharmacy Benefit fill history records as rejected at the pharmacy, with a fill date in the counting window.

**Which window applies?** The counting window: the number of months in the category's cap period counted back from the review date, a date counting when it lies fewer than that many whole months before the review date.

**Does a rejected fill below the refill minimum matter?** No. With fewer than 5 paid refills in the window there is no medication relief, whether or not any fill was rejected.

## Readings at the boundary (hypothetical fill histories)

| Paid refills in the window | Rejected fills in the window | Medication relief credit |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0 | 60.00 USD |
| 7 | 1 | 30.00 USD |
| 4 | 0 | None |
| 4 | 2 | None |
| 6 | 0, with one rejected fill dated before the window | 60.00 USD |
